loText: Calculate and evaluate one or two iterations of interim cashflows in a three-tiered securitization structure.
question:
A manager of collateralized loan obligations (CLOs) is reviewing the performance of a CLO that has a pool of 50 identical loans, each priced at its par value of GBP 1 million. The underlying loan assets are floating-rate obligations that pay a fixed spread of 150 bps over LIBOR. The coupons and interest payments on the following liabilities are made on an annual basis and occur at the end of the year:

|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
| Liabilities | Amount (GBP) | Coupon |
| Senior debt | 37,500,000 | LIBOR + 45 bps |
| Mezzanine debt | 10,000,000 | LIBOR + 300 bps |
| Equity | 2,500,000 |  |

|  |  |
|---|---|
| The manager reports that the CLO initially has no overcollateralization, and the |  |
| annual excess spread flowing into the overcollateralization account has a limit of |  |
| GBD 250,000. Suppose the LIBOR curve remains flat at 4% in the first year, and |  |
| assuming no defaults in the collateral pool and no management and transaction |  |
| fees, what are the correct amounts that the manager would post to the |  |
| overcollateralization account and to the equity tranche after the first year? |  |
| Overcollateralization Account | Equity Tranche |
solution:
**Concept**

Securitisation waterfall. Interest from the collateral pays the senior coupon, then the mezzanine coupon. What is left is excess spread. Excess spread goes to the overcollateralisation account up to its annual limit, and the remainder goes to equity.

**Working**

**Collateral interest:** 50,000,000 × (4% + 1.5%) = 2,750,000

**Senior coupon:** 37,500,000 × 4.45% = 1,668,750

**Mezzanine coupon:** 10,000,000 × 7% = 700,000

**Excess spread:** 2,750,000 − 1,668,750 − 700,000 = 381,250

**Overcollateralisation account:** min(381,250, 250,000) = 250,000

**Equity:** 381,250 − 250,000 = 131,250

**Exam trap.** Order of the waterfall: the overcollateralisation account is filled first, up to its cap, and equity takes the residual. Options B and D each send the whole excess spread to […]

loText: Calculate and evaluate one or two iterations of interim cashflows in a three-tiered securitization structure.
question:
A manager from the structured credit risk desk at a bank is presenting to a group of newly hired risk analysts on calculating cash flows in a securitization structure. The manager illustrates the procedure with the existing collateral pool of loans and the corresponding liabilities, all with a maturity of 5 years, using the following information:

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Initial number of loans in the collateral pool | 100 |
| Principal amount of each loan | EUR 1,000,000 |
| Total coupon interest to be paid annually on all junior |  |
| EUR 6,300,000 |  |
| and senior bonds |  |
| Maximum annual amount flowing from the excess |  |
| EUR 1,500,000 |  |
| spread into the overcollateralization account |  |
| Swap rate per year for all maturities | 3.5% |
| Recovery rate in the event of a loan default | 45% |

The manager makes additional observations as follows:

- The loans in the collateral pool pay a fixed spread of 2.2% over the swap curve.
- There were no defaults in year 1.
- The value of the overcollateralization account at the end of year 1 was EUR 0.

What is the value of the overcollateralization account at the end of year 2 if there are 8 defaults in year 2?
solution:
**Concept**

The overcollateralisation account grows with excess spread (up to a cap) and with recoveries on defaulted loans, and it is drawn down to cover interest shortfalls. $\text{OC}_{t} = (1 + \text{swap rate}) \text{OC}_{t-1} +$ recoveries + excess spread deposited (or less shortfall paid).

**Working**

**Year 1:** interest = 5.7% × 100,000,000 = 5,700,000 \< 6,300,000. No excess spread, so the account ends year 1 at zero.

**Year 2 interest:** 5.7% × 92 × 1,000,000 = 5,244,000

**Shortfall:** 5,244,000 − 6,300,000 = −1,056,000

**Recoveries:** 0.45 × 8 × 1,000,000 = 3,600,000

**Account at end of year 2:** $3{,}600{,}000 - 1{,}056{,}000 = \text{EUR} 2{,}544{,}000$

loText: Explain how the default probabilities and default correlations affect the credit risk in a securitization.
question: A financial firm has sold default protection on the most senior tranche of a CDO. If the default correlation between assets held in the CDO decreases sharply from the correlation used in pricing the CDO tranches, assuming everything else is unchanged, how will the position of the financial firm be impacted?

options.A: It will either increase or decrease, depending on the pricing model used and the market conditions.
options.B: It will gain significant value, since the probability of exercising the protection falls.
options.C: It will lose significant value, since the protection will gain value.
options.D: It will neither gain nor lose value, since only expected default losses matter and correlation does not affect expected default losses.

solution:
**Concept**

The senior tranche suffers only if many assets default together. Lower default correlation makes clustered defaults less likely, so the senior tranche becomes safer. A seller of protection on the senior tranche gains when the tranche’s risk falls.

**Exam trap.** Senior tranches are short correlation; equity tranches are long correlation. Then fix the position: a protection seller gains when the tranche gets safer.

loText: Explain how the default probabilities and default correlations affect the credit risk in a securitization.
question: An investment firm is contemplating taking positions in various tranches of a collateralized debt obligation. The chief CDO analyst at the firm predicts that the default probability will increase significantly and that default correlation will decrease. On this basis, the analyst will most likely recommend the:

options.A: Purchase of the senior tranche and sale of the equity tranche
options.B: Purchase of the equity tranche and sale of the senior tranche
options.C: Purchase of the senior tranche and purchase of the equity tranche
options.D: Sale of the senior tranche and sale of the equity tranche

solution:
**Concept**

Equity tranche: hurt by higher default probability, helped by higher correlation (high correlation makes “no defaults at all” more likely, so the equity holder is long correlation). Senior tranche: hurt by higher correlation (clustered defaults are what can reach it), so it is short correlation.

**Exam trap.** The two tranches have opposite correlation exposures. Fix one sentence: “equity is long correlation, senior is short correlation”.

loText: Explain how the default probabilities and default correlations affect the credit risk in a securitization.
question: An investment firm has sold default protection on the most senior tranche of a collateralized debt obligation. Suppose the default correlation between assets held in the CDO increases sharply, but everything else remains unchanged. How will the firm’s position be affected?

options.A: It will neither lose nor gain value because correlation does not affect default losses
options.B: It will lose significant value, since the probability of exercising the protection increases
options.C: It will either increase or decrease depending on market conditions
options.D: It will gain significant value because the probability of exercising the protection falls

solution:
**Concept**

The senior tranche is damaged only if many assets default together. Higher default correlation makes clustered defaults more likely, so it raises the risk of the senior tranche. A seller of protection on that tranche is long the tranche’s credit and so loses when its risk rises.

**Exam trap.** Polarity and position. The existing bank question asks the same thing with correlation falling, where the seller gains. Here correlation rises and the seller loses.

loText: Define securitization, describe the securitization process, and explain the role of participants in the process.
question: A bank is planning to securitize car loans using an SPV. The bank would sell the loans to an SPV through a “true sale” and the SPV would issue securities under a “revolving securitization structure.” As part of its planning, the bank is reviewing characteristics of securitization transactions in general as well as specific features that are commonly incorporated into revolving structures. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The credit quality of the securitized car loan assets would be enhanced if the principal value of securities issued is higher than the principal value of the assets.
options.B: The SPV can provide the bank with a funding advantage if the credit quality of the securitized car loan assets is higher than the credit quality of the bank’s balance sheet.
options.C: Under a revolving structure, prepayment assumptions are not incorporated, which typically results in principal amounts paid to investors on a coupon-by-coupon basis throughout the life of the security.
options.D: Under a revolving structure, the bank transfers the car loan assets to the SPV and the SPV can issue multiple securitizations, which are priced and traded based on weighted-average life of the structure as well as on investor demand.

solution:
**Concept**

Securitisation moves assets to a special purpose vehicle that funds itself by issuing notes. Motives include cheaper funding, balance sheet relief and risk transfer. Structures: amortising (principal passed through as received), revolving (principal reinvested during a revolving period, then repaid) and master trust (one vehicle issuing multiple series).

**Exam trap.** Overcollateralisation means the notes issued are smaller than the asset pool. Options C and D attach the features of amortising and master trust structures to the revolving label.

**Learning objectives tested:** CR-23a, CR-23c, CR-23d.

loText: Define securitization, describe the securitization process, and explain the role of participants in the process.
question: A bank is planning to securitize car loans by creating an SPV. The bank would sell the loans to an SPV through a “true sale” and the SPV would issue securities under a “revolving securitization structure.” The project manager for this task is reviewing characteristics of securitization transactions in general as well as specific features that are commonly incorporated into revolving structures. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The credit quality of the securitized car loan assets would be enhanced if the principal value of securities issued is higher than the principal value of the assets.
options.B: The SPV can allow the bank to access cheaper funding if the credit quality of the securitized car loan assets is higher than the credit quality of the bank’s balance sheet.
options.C: Under a revolving structure, prepayment assumptions are not incorporated, which typically results in principal amounts paid to investors through a series of coupons over the lifetime of the security.
options.D: Under a revolving structure, the bank transfers the car loan assets to the SPV and the SPV can issue multiple securitizations, which are priced and traded based on weighted-average life of the structure.

solution:
**Concept**

Same structures as the previous question. Cheaper funding is available when the securitised assets are of better credit quality than the originator’s balance sheet as a whole, so the notes carry a higher rating than the bank itself.

**Exam trap.** Prepayment assumptions drive the pricing of amortising structures through the weighted-average life. Pricing on weighted-average life is an amortising feature, not a revolving one.

loText: Define and calculate the delinquency ratio, default ratio, monthly payment rate (MPR), debt service coverage ratio (DSCR), the weighted average coupon (WAC), the weighted average maturity (WAM), and the weighted average life (WAL) for relevant securitized structures.
question:
A financial analyst is calculating the weighted average life (WAL) of the loans in an MBS pool. The initial notional value outstanding of the MBS pool is USD 50 million. The payment schedule and the assumed pool factor for the MBS are provided in the table below:

|  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Coupon | Principal |  |  |  |
| payment | Actual | payment |  |  |
| date | Dates | days | Pool factor | (USD million) |
| 0 | November 21, 2023 | 66 | 1.00 | – |
| 1 | January 26, 2024 | 181 | 0.76 | 12 |
| 2 | July 26, 2024 | 184 | 0.54 | 11 |
| 3 | January 26, 2025 | 183 | 0.38 | 8 |
| 4 | July 25, 2025 | 182 | 0.26 | 6 |
| 5 | January 24, 2026 | 183 | 0.18 | 4 |
| 6 | July 25, 2026 | – | – | 9 |

Assuming coupon payments are made semi-annually and there are 365 days in a year, what is the WAL of the MBS pool?
solution:
**Concept**

Weighted-average life is the average time a unit of principal remains outstanding: WAL = $\sum\frac{\text{days in period}}{365} \times$ pool factor at the start of the period.

**Working**

| Period | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Days | 66 | 181 | 184 | 183 | 182 | 183 |
| Pool factor | 1.00 | 0.76 | 0.54 | 0.38 | 0.26 | 0.18 |
| Days × factor | 66.00 | 137.56 | 99.36 | 69.54 | 47.32 | 32.94 |

WAL $= \frac{66.00 + 137.56 + 99.36 + 69.54 + 47.32 + 32.94}{365} = \frac{452.72}{365} = 1.24$ years

**Exam trap.** The first period is a short stub of 66 days and is easy to drop. WAL must be well below final maturity because most of the principal is repaid early.
